accuracy.evidence: Matches KS1 ocean idea: vast salt water, shore/shallow/deep, waves, habitat; puddles/pools/baths excluded; distinct from water-locations list.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets puddle/bath/pool=ocean, fresh-ocean, whale-on-land, and tiny-ocean myths in sort, salt, homes, challenge why(), and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab defines what the ocean is (zones, salt, habitat, waves) — distinct from where-water-is-found mapping (flagwater) and living-things needs (flagneeds).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner builds zones, sorts ocean vs not, marks salt/fresh, places whale home, shows waves and vast size before confirmation text.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (puddle/bathtub as ocean; fresh ocean; whale in field; pool=ocean) are overturned by sort/salt/homes tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names puddle/bath/same, fresh/juice, sand/field/toy, saltier pool, under/rock, and whales/metal slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 5–7 wording: short kid lines, shore/shallow/deep and salty/fresh named plainly.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches ocean definition, habitat, or a myth to reject.

mobile.evidence: Large zone and sort buttons; tap twins for drag; challenge stack usable at phone width.

accessibility.evidence: Zones, sort, salt, homes, waves, and idea steps expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum Geography KS1: name and locate the world’s oceans; understand geographical similarities
UK National Curriculum Science KS1: animals in their habitats; everyday materials — water
BBC Bitesize KS1 / National Geographic Kids: oceans as large salt-water bodies and habitats
